burns.why: You put something of yours down to them.
You blamed them in the Lessons Learned Review, in the minutes.
You gave them your word, and broke it.
You reported them at the Listening Session, in complete confidence.
You started a rumour about them.
You moved them to the desk with no window.
You passed them over for the bonus.
You hired a friend over the person they recommended.
You tried to get them fired, and they found out.
You left them out of your team's bonus pot, and signed a letter about resilience.
You sat them by the lift, for questioning your plans.
You split them up from the person they sat with, because they talked.
You drew their line out of your team at the Org Design Workshop.
You paid for your consultant out of their training budget.
Your consultant presented their work back to them, as a framework.
You put them on call over the bank holiday, for questioning your plans.
You cut the checks they run, to meet a cut, and kept the plan as it was.
You passed the Chief Financial Officer's cut down to them.
You had them write the Board's offsite deck overnight.
You presented the deck they wrote overnight as your own.
You put your figure down to them, in front of the Board.

became.practitioner: Learnt how things really work here, and became a Practitioner
became.whistleblower: Started keeping a file, and became a whistleblower

signs.text: {who} writes down the time whenever you speak, and underlines it.
signs.clue: {who} has started writing down the time whenever you speak.

signs.text: {who} forwards something to their personal address, and closes the laptop when you look over.
{who} asks for that in writing, please, and smiles while asking.

whistleblower.motive: {who} had been keeping a file on you, and took it upstairs.

bill.title: The schedule
bill.body: Your boss's boss would like a word about the schedule you sent upstairs. Somebody has been to see them with a folder, and the folder has the real dates in it. Your boss's boss does not say who. They say that they are not angry, which is how you know.

bill.title: Your status reports
bill.body: Your boss's boss has been sent your Monthly Status Reports, side by side with what actually happened, in two colours. They would like you to talk them through the green ones. There are a lot of green ones.

bill.title: A brief, informal conversation, recorded
bill.body: Human Resources would like a brief, informal conversation about some concerns that have been raised, informally, in a document of eleven pages. They cannot say who raised them. The document has a contents page.

notice.title: Dennis Prowse has left
notice.body: The Team Leader has left, after a long and frank conversation with nobody in particular. An all-staff e-mail thanks Dennis for his leadership and says he is leaving to spend more time with his principles. His mug has been left on his desk, which nobody will sit at until the seat is filled.

notice.title: Priya Venn has left
notice.body: The Senior Analyst has left, with a week's notice and most of a carrot cake. An all-staff email thanks Priya for her contribution and says she is leaving to pursue other opportunities. An agency temp has been given her desk, her login and her figures, and has been told the figures are self-explanatory.

notice.title: Marjorie Tull has left
notice.body: The Office Co-ordinator has left after twenty-six years, taking the key to the stationery cupboard and the knowledge of where everything is kept. An interim has started. The interim has been told where nothing is kept, and is writing it down.

notice.title: Callum Reed has left
notice.body: The Project Co-ordinator has left. A contractor is now co-ordinating your project at a day rate, from home, and the Monthly Status Report's figures now arrive on time, from a template. Nobody has checked them, and nobody can now say who would have.

notice.title: Tessa Croft has left
notice.body: The Junior Associate has left for a role with a longer title at a smaller company. A new Junior Associate starts on Monday, and has already asked for the figures, and how you did them.

notice.title: Hugh Lamb has left
notice.body: The Head of Operations has left, after a review of priorities in which Operations was not one. An all-staff e-mail thanks Hugh for his stewardship, and says he is leaving to take up a portfolio career. An acting Head of Operations has been found, and has been told it is acting.
